<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
  <meta charset="UTF-8">
  <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0">
  <meta name="color-scheme" content="light">
  <meta name="theme-color" content="#fff">
  <meta name="description" content="A single black circle centered on a white page.">
  <title>Black circle</title>
  <style>
    *, *::before, *::after {
      box-sizing: border-box;
      margin: 0;
      padding: 0;
    }
    body {
      min-height: 100vh;
      min-height: 100dvh;
      display: grid;
      place-items: center;
      background: #fff;
    }
    svg {
      display: block;
      width: min(400px, 90vmin);
      height: auto;
    }
    @media (forced-colors: active) {
      circle { fill: CanvasText; }
    }
  </style>
  <link rel="icon" href="data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' viewBox='0 0 2 2'%3E%3Ccircle cx='1' cy='1' r='1'/%3E%3C/svg%3E">
</head>
<body>
  <main>
    <svg width="400" height="400" viewBox="0 0 400 400" role="img" aria-labelledby="circle-title">
      <title id="circle-title">Black circle</title>
      <circle cx="200" cy="200" r="200" fill="#000"/>
    </svg>
  </main>
</body>
</html>

content.text:
I made no changes to `0.html` because it's already in good shape. It's a small page that shows one black circle in the middle of a white page, and it already covers the basics:

- **Layout:** the circle stays centered with correct sizing on mobile, and it scales down to fit small screens.
- **Accessibility:** screen readers get a label for the circle, and it stays visible in Windows high-contrast mode.
- **Page details:** it has a page description and a matching circle icon for the browser tab.

Anything else I could change would be a matter of taste rather than a fix. To go further I'd need to know what you're after, for example:

1. **Dark mode:** show a white circle on black when the system is set to dark.
2. **Animation:** make the circle pulse or grow, while respecting the setting that reduces motion.
3. **Different content:** if the circle is a placeholder, tell me what the page should actually be.

Which direction do you want, or was there something specific that bothered you?
